svg.aria-label: Detail map of the Wuyue kingdom around Hangzhou

g.data-info: The Wuyue capital, walled and expanded by Qian Liu.
Built by Qian Chu c. 975; its bricks held rolls of a printed dhāraṇī sutra, found when the pagoda collapsed in 1924.
The tide wall of 910, the setting for the legend of King Qian shooting arrows at the bore.
Wuyue’s largest northern prefecture, on the shore of Lake Tai.
Modern Shaoxing; the Yue kilns nearby made the celadon “secret colour” wares sent as tribute.
Modern Ningbo, the port for Korea and Japan.
Birthplace of the Tiantai school. The Wuyue court asked Goryeo and Japan to send back its lost texts.
Island shrine to Guanyin; tradition dates it to a Japanese monk c. 916.
Western prefecture on the upper Qiantang.
Taken by Wuyue in 947 after the fall of Min.
Capital of the rival Southern Tang.
